title: Market-to-book Ratio in Stochastic Portfolio Theory

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper develops functionally generated portfolios in the context of Stochastic Portfolio Theory (SPT) using auxiliary economic variables such as book values and market-to-book ratios. Portfolios are constructed using both additive and multiplicative generation frameworks based on market weights, relative book values, and ranks of market-to-book ratios. Empirical tests are conducted on daily closing prices and year-end annual book values for the 500 largest stocks in capitalization from Compustat North America.
extraction.universe: 500 largest stocks in capitalization from the Compustat North America database on January 1, 2001

key_findings: Functionally generated portfolios depending on auxiliary variables like book values can successfully incorporate the value factor into Stochastic Portfolio Theory.

Equally-weighted portfolios composed of stocks selected by market-to-book ratios outperform the market, with higher returns generated by investing in stocks with lower market-to-book ratios (growth/value distinction).
Empirical comparisons indicate that the value factor exhibits a slightly milder effect on portfolio performance than the size factor in the tested universe.
limitations: The stock selection is subject to survivorship bias as it relies on the d = 500 largest stocks in capitalization on the first trading day (2001 January 1st).
